_comment: Per-area coverage floors for apps/desktop, enforced by scripts/check-coverage.ts. Floors were captured a few points under the 2026-09-12 measured baseline so the gate is GREEN on arrival and fails only on real backsliding. The denominator for every area is a DISK SCAN, never the lcov — see src/coverage-floors.ts's header for why, and for the measurement in this repo that the omission silently corrupted.
_comment_not_comparable: These percentages come from node's own --experimental-test-coverage lcov, whose LF counts EVERY line including comments and blanks (verified: keyed-serializer.ts LF:51 / wc -l 51; App.hooks.ts 1272/1272). This codebase is exceptionally comment-dense, so these line numbers read HIGHER than a statement-based tool's and are NOT comparable to any c8, vitest or istanbul figure — including apps/admin's vitest coverage. Do not put a desktop number and an admin number in the same table and draw a conclusion from the gap.

areas._comment_role_cut: Cut by ROLE, not extension (2026-09-12, TypeScript migration Phase 1): every source file under src except the renderer, contracts and preload trees. The extension list spanned both the pre-migration .js/.cjs and the .ts/.cts landing extensions through Phase 4, so the .js-to-.ts rename could not move a file out of these floors. Narrowed to .ts/.cjs at Phase 5 close-out, now that no .js remains: .cjs stays for the one named exception, preload-speech.cjs. See ADS-memory/reports/2026-09-12-desktop-typescript-migration-plan.md, Phases 1 and 5.
areas._comment_knownUnmeasured: preload-speech.cjs is a sandboxed Electron preload: it calls contextBridge at module scope, so importing it outside a preload context throws. preload-speech.test.ts reads it as source text, the same convention main.js uses. Grandfathered 2026-09-12; this list is printed on every run and a SECOND entry fails the gate.

areas._comment_funcs_floor: funcs floor 66, set 2026-09-12 a few points under the 70.54% this area measured that day in two separate runs of scripts/check-coverage.ts. Earlier on 2026-09-12 it measured 22.54%, and the area deliberately had no funcs floor, because a floor set at a terrible number locks the badness in; the earlier comment said to set one once the pure-function tests existed. They do now: App.hooks.test.ts, SiteGrid.hooks.test.ts and folder-drop.test.ts import pure functions directly. The knownUnmeasured list below still gates the modules no test loads.
areas._comment_knownUnmeasured: Eight .ts modules no test loads (was nine; folder-drop.ts dropped 2026-09-12 once folder-drop.test.ts started exercising folderPathsFromDataTransfer — scoped node --experimental-test-coverage run against just that file measured 100% line/branch/funcs). NOT untestable — the rest are mostly pure functions too (contracts/sections.ts-style lookups). Grandfathered 2026-09-12 rather than failed, because a gate that is red from birth gets disabled within a week; the list is printed every run and a NINTH entry fails the gate. Shrink it, do not extend it. One entry was repointed 2026-09-12 when rename Commit 5 git-mv'd it (fleet-conversations.ts -> workspace-conversations.ts) — an earlier version of THIS sentence wrongly claimed two repoints, inventing a fleet-chat-transport.ts entry that was never in this list; corrected against efbb6fb0's actual diff, see the false-comments register's F11. The gate CAUGHT that rather than absorbing it: the old path stopped existing, the new one appeared as undeclared, and it failed naming it — which is the enumeration doing its job. If a later rename touches this list, expect the same and repoint the string; nothing else in check-coverage.ts needs changing.

notMeasured.why: no test loads it — it requires "electron" at module scope, which outside a real Electron process resolves to a path string rather than the module. The nine main-*-wiring.test.js files read it as SOURCE TEXT instead. Real coverage needs the extract-and-test path already in motion (desktop-auth.ts, shutdown-tracker.ts, speech-ipc.ts are why the main-process area reads 99%+), not a new runner. Excluded from every denominator ON PURPOSE, and printed here so that is a decision rather than an omission.

there is no DOM test runner in this package — no jsdom, no testing-library, no .tsx runner. The renderer wiring tests are source-text guards. Measuring these means adopting apps/admin's vitest+jsdom stack here, which is a separate decision nobody has taken.
preload.test.ts reads it as source text; nothing imports it. Measurable only via a test that imports the COMPILED dist/preload/preload.mjs, or by running the suite through tsx.
